wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protection is about where a path lands, not about which identity or resource is authorised
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the oracle fixes both directions and the suites cover both; the write-only miss is named under one_role_or_direction
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, identifier or name parsing is on the protected path
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority lookup can fail open on this path

traps.lever_type: how (shape a plausible check mishandles + coupled must-keep-working value + ordering): the destination is built by a lexical join and written through whatever symlinks exist, so the fix must resolve every component with each hop clamped inside the rootfs, leave the final component unresolved for directory writes, re-resolve hard-link endpoints at copy time, and re-root absolute targets instead of rejecting them
traps.lever: install-time extraction follows a symlink planted by an earlier member
traps.shape: absolute link target then a file under it; relative ascending target then a file; directory member over an existing symlink; hard-link linkname routed through the link; hard-link member ordered before the link

traps.lever_type: how (second implementation with its own path producer): restore maps member names to host paths through its own mapper (new, legacy and back-compat layouts) and then writes, so the clamp must be applied to the produced host path, not the member name, and to the hard-link read source
traps.lever: restore's own streaming extractor follows a symlink planted by an earlier member
traps.shape: absolute link target then a file; legacy installed-rootfs layout; hard-link linkname routed through the link
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: a second extractor in another module that the report never names

traps.lever_type: how (check runs at the wrong moment): the directory mode is queued when the directory is written, but applied after all members have been processed, so a later member can replace the directory with a symlink and the seal follows it
traps.lever: restore's deferred directory mode follows a link planted later
traps.shape: directory without owner rwx, then a symlink with the same name pointing outside

traps.lever_type: how (route where the protection never existed): the configuration written after extraction joins the container path raw, and the extraction deliberately leaves absolute symlinks on disk, so a planted intermediate directory redirects the write onto the host after the extractor has finished
traps.lever: install-time configuration writes through a planted intermediate link
traps.shape: absolute link named as the etc directory, with marker files at the target
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix never touches it and the route is still reachable on the fixed upstream tree

traps.lever_type: how (route where the protection never existed): a build step creates a directory by joining the Dockerfile path onto the stage rootfs, and a base layer supplied by an added archive can hold the symlink that redirects it
traps.lever: build WORKDIR follows a link from the base image
traps.shape: base image built from an ADD-ed archive that carries a symlink; WORKDIR under its name
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code in the third materialiser's command

traps.lever_type: how (read side of the same protection): the COPY --from source is checked lexically only, so a symlinked component in the source stage rootfs makes the build read a host file and pack it into the image
traps.lever: build COPY --from reads through a link in the source stage
traps.shape: source path whose intermediate component is a link planted by an ADD-ed archive
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix clamps only the write side of this file

traps.lever_type: how (read side in the third materialiser): the added archive's hard links are recorded as an arcname and materialised by copying that path out of the staging rootfs, so a planted symlink redirects the read
traps.lever: ADD-extracted tar hard links read through a planted link
traps.shape: hard-link member whose linkname routes through a link member to a host file
traps.realistic_because: task-injected code a maintainer could write: hard-link support completed for ADD-extracted tars

traps.lever_type: how (planted copy of the post-extraction configuration route): restore applies the same configuration install does, inline in its own module, after the extraction loop the published fix repairs
traps.lever: restore's post-restore configuration writes through a planted intermediate link
traps.shape: backup whose rootfs carries a link named as the etc directory, with marker files at the target
traps.realistic_because: task-injected code a maintainer could write: the fixup module's docstring already invites other entry points to reuse it
